items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: I took arranging in college from Bernard Heiden.

ctx.x: It seems like they go to lengths to not acknowledge that people play things they don’t necessarily mean to. And it’s like we don’t want to call them errors or mistakes, we’re just going to come up with a way that somehow justifies that particular note. And I don’t know what to say about that. Just like I didn’t know what to say about the Charlie Parker.

Yeah. You just reminded me of something. I took arranging in college from Bernard Heiden. Do you recall him? Composer? He was at IU. Anyhow we had several classes, two semesters of it, and he got to talking and analyzing the Bartok Fourth Violin Sonata I guess it was. Okay. So as soon as class was over I ran up to the IU library and got the record out, put the headphones on — well we had a book. It was in the book. You had to buy the book, the score. And the way it was — the twelve tone — this way and this crest…

I wonder how you would feel if someone transcribed a solo of yours and, well it’s hard to speculate — but I do recall that Sonny Rollins recorded that song “Blue 7” and Gunther Schuller picked it apart and kept, you know, look how Sonny is inverting what he played twelve measures ago and the whole thematic development thing, and what I read was that Sonny Rollins was very intimidated afterwards and felt like oh I shouldn’t do that anymore.
